summary.text: Bret Cecil is the Democratic candidate for Oregon House of Representatives District 1 in the November 3, 2026 general election, where he faces Republican incumbent Court Boice.
Cecil lives in Port Orford, chairs the Curry County Democratic Party, and has run for the seat before.

paragraphs.text: Bret Cecil was born in Long Beach, California, and earned a high school diploma from Los Alamitos High School.

His listed career experience includes work as a farmer and rancher, veterinary assistant, medical records technician and transcriber, personal trainer and fitness instructor, property owner and manager, and builder and small-scale developer.

In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, Cecil said he has lived in Port Orford, Curry County, for nearly ten years and described himself as a community organizer and volunteer, chair of the Curry County Democratic Party, a delegate to the Democratic Party of Oregon, and immediate past chair of its Stonewall Caucus.
He also said he is a budget committee member of the South Coast Education Services District and a member of the Coos/Curry Transit Advisory Board.

Cecil was the Democratic nominee for House District 1 in 2022, when incumbent David Brock Smith won with 70.5 percent of the vote to his 29.2 percent, and again in 2024, when Boice won with 67.2 percent to his 32.5 percent.
He advanced from the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 98.0 percent of the vote.

In the 2026 survey, Cecil said he would hold annual in-person town hall meetings in the district, support Oregon's vote-by-mail system, and support campaign finance reform, and that he does not accept corporate contributions.
He named housing; health, behavioral, child and elder care; education; and transportation as the policy areas he is most passionate about.
